speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia alongside a significant medical history; to understand the root cause, please describe your past diagnoses and current symptoms in detail. Additionally, will you be able to walk a straight line or stand with your feet together?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing your "drunken" gait and right-sided clumsiness; to determine if this is a central nervous system issue, does the ataxia worsen when you close your eyes or look at a target with your eyes open? REQUEST TEST: Romberg_Test; REQUEST TEST: Ophthalmologic_Exam.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results showing normal readings are surprising given your symptoms; does the ataxia improve when you fix your gaze on a stationary object, and have you noticed any changes in your handwriting or speech clarity? REQUEST TEST: Oculomotor_Exam; REQUEST TEST: Cerebellar_Function_Scale.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Oculomotor_Exam: No nystagmus observed; saccadic movements normal; smooth pursuit intact. Cerebellar_Function_Scale: Score 2/10 (Severe deficits); inability to perform finger-to-nose test bilaterally, significant dysmetria noted on heel-to-shin maneuver, and intention tremor present.

speaker: Doctor
text: The severe cerebellar deficits confirm a central nervous system issue, but since your eye movements and Romberg test were normal, I suspect the lesion is supratentorial rather than in the vestibulocerebellum. Have you noticed any changes in your balance or coordination when you are lying down with your eyes closed, or does this happen only when standing or walking? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain with Cerebellar protocol.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI confirms multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, which is pathognomonic for PML. Given your history of significant medical issues, I strongly suspect an underlying immunocompromised state, such as HIV or immunosuppressive therapy, which has predisposed you to this opportunistic infection. Do you have a history of HIV, organ transplant, or current use of immunosuppressive medications?
